name: Self-refine and cascade answers with TypeSafe Jev
description: A cheap model answers first and TypeSafe Jev judges every answer: does it answer the question, is it physically plausible, how helpful is it. A rejected answer goes back to the cheap model with Jev's feedback (self-refine); after two rejected attempts the question escalates to a stronger model (cascade). Built on the Graph flow control, which lets a step jump back to one that already ran.
shortDescription: Judge every AI answer with TypeSafe Jev, retry with feedback, and escalate to a stronger model only when needed.
keyFeatures: Self-refine: a rejected answer goes back to the model with Jev's feedback on what failed
Cascade: a cheap model answers first, a strong model only after two rejected attempts
One Jev call judges each answer on three typed questions: relevance, plausibility and helpfulness
Built on the Graph flow control, with a retry counter and a transition budget
prerequisites: A ByteChef version with the Graph flow control
A TypeSafe AI API key (https://typesafe.ai) in a TypeSafe AI connection
An Anthropic connection for the cheap and the strong model
idealFor: Teams that want AI answers checked before anyone sees them, without paying for the largest model on every request.
steps: Trigger: run the workflow manually with a question.
Count the attempt and answer with the cheap model.
Ask TypeSafe Jev whether the answer addresses the question, is plausible and is helpful.
If it passes, keep the answer. If not, turn the verdict into feedback and let the cheap model try again.
After two rejected attempts, answer with the strong model, using the same feedback.
